newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South Africa spells out tax holiday proposals.
newsitem.headline: South Africa spells out tax holiday proposals.

text.p: The Department of Finance has spelled out the rules for tax holidays of up to six years in accordance with Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's macroeconomic strategy for growth, employment and redistribution.
The rules are outlined in a draft explanatory memorandum to a Revenue Laws Amendment Bill set for debate by the National Assembly on September 11.
A Finance Ministry official said the bill would be put to parliament's finance committee at an informal meeting on Monday and could be amended before its formal submission to parliament on Wednesday.
But the official pointed out: "This is a money bill, which means that parliament has no formal right to amend it. They can only accept it or reject it."
The document details tax holidays of up to two years each based on the location, industry or job creation potential of manufacturing projects launched after October 1 this year.
"A qualifying company may therefore become eligible for tax holiday status for a maximum period of six years," the memorandum says.

"The purpose of the tax holiday scheme is to encourage the establishment of new businesses in South Africa and it is therefore not desirable that an existing business be transferred into projects in order to obtain the concession and reduce the existing national normal tax base."
- The company or close corporation must be established solely for the single approved project and approval must be given before the project is launched.

- The holiday applies only to taxable income and the full benefit must be taken up within 10 years of the project's launch, which means companies that do not achieve profitability soon could forfeit part of the tax benefit.
- The ministers of finance and trade and industry will together set investment requirements, identify geographic areas to be promoted and define industries likely to promote economic growth.

Factors affecting location will include potential to strengthen secondary cities, to reinforce urban nodes along development corridors, to consolidate emerging centres of infrastructure and to promote the diversification of local economies.
Target industries will be selected according to their potential to contribute to economic growth, their employment potential and the international demand for the product.
Tax holidays based on human resource development will be subject to retrospective verification.
If a company wins a two year exemption on the basis of job creation and another factor, the human resource incentive will be deemed to cover the final two years of the holiday.
The bill includes provision for the withdrawal of tax holidays in the case of fraud, including transfer pricing.
